mainTopic: Does a מצוה need כוונה? רבא holds it does not. The גמרא tests this against several sources and against בל תוסיף, and ends with רבא's rule about when breaking a מצוה needs כוונה.
overview: Just before this amud, רבא ruled that someone who blew שופר only to make music still fulfilled the מצוה. The גמרא explains why this needed saying and concludes that רבא holds מצוות אין צריכות כוונה. Challenges from a משנה about reading שמע, our own משנה about hearing שופר outside the בית הכנסת, and a ברייתא about the blower's intent are all pushed off. In each case, the only intent needed is to do the act properly, not intent to fulfill the מצוה. אביי then asks: if so, why isn't sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת a violation of בל תוסיף? רבא answers that בל תוסיף applies only during a מצוה's time. רב שמן בר אבא challenges this from a כהן adding his own blessing to ברכת כהנים, and the גמרא answers that the whole day is that מצוה's time. It then tries to prove this idea from a משנה about mixed blood of קרבנות. Finally, רבא gives his settled rule: fulfilling a מצוה needs no כוונה, breaking it during its time needs no כוונה, and breaking it outside its time does need כוונה.

steps.title: Why רבא's שופר ruling was needed
steps.stepSummary: By שופר the פסוק says 'זכרון תרועה', which sounds like it needs awareness, and this person was just going through the motions. So רבא had to teach that he still fulfills the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, by שופר, the פסוק says 'a remembrance of blasts', and this person was just acting without any awareness. So רבא needed to teach us that he still fulfills it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering the question 'Why did רבא need to say this? It is obvious from the case of מצה!' It explains that שופר is different and needed its own teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מצה, the תורה said 'eat מצה', and he did eat, so the act itself is what counts. By שופר, the תורה calls the מצוה a 'זכרון', a remembrance, which suggests the mind must be involved. Since a music-player is only a מתעסק, you might think he does not fulfill the obligation. רבא teaches that he does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A remembrance of blasts', the תורה's description of the day of שופר
Someone acting without awareness or intent, just going through the motions
'It teaches us', the point the teaching comes to add

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the beginning of a new discussion. It is the second half of an answer that began before this section, comparing שופר to the case of being forced to eat מצה.

phrases.english: But here, 'a remembrance of blasts' is written,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:24

phrases.english: and this one is merely acting without awareness —
so it teaches us [that he still fulfills it].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are not in the text, but the גמרא assumes them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the earlier question of why רבא's ruling was needed, given the case of מצה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: שופר has a special פסוק that suggests awareness is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of 'זכרון', you might think someone blowing שופר without intent does not fulfill the מצוה
steps.terutzMaskana: Even by שופר, a person acting without intent still fulfills the obligation

steps.title: רבא holds מצוות do not need intent
steps.stepSummary: From רבא's ruling, the גמרא concludes that he holds מצוות אין צריכות כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that רבא holds that מצוות do not require intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general rule out of רבא's specific ruling about שופר. This sets up the challenges that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a music-player, with no thought of the מצוה at all, fulfills שופר, then רבא must hold that intent is never needed. This turns one case into a big principle. Everything that follows tests whether this principle can survive.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Apparently' or 'it follows that', introducing a conclusion
מצוות do not need intent to fulfill them
Intent, here meaning intent to fulfill the מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether מצוות צריכות כוונה is one of the most famous questions in the גמרא, and it matters in practice for every מצוה a person does.

phrases.english: Apparently, Rava holds:
מצוות do not require intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from the explanation of רבא's ruling in step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא holds מצוות אין צריכות כוונה

steps.title: Challenge from reading שמע in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that someone reading the שמע section in the תורה when the time for קריאת שמע arrives fulfills the obligation only if he 'directed his heart'. Doesn't that mean intent to fulfill the מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If someone was reading the תורה and the time for saying שמע arrived, if he directed his heart he fulfilled it, and if not, he did not. Doesn't 'directed his heart' mean he intended to fulfill the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's principle with a משנה that seems to require intent. It suggests the משנה's 'directed his heart' means intent to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person here is already saying the words of שמע. If he still does not fulfill the מצוה without 'directing his heart', the simple reading is that he needs intent to fulfill. That would mean מצוות צריכות כוונה, against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They challenged him', bringing a source against a statement
The time for reciting קריאת שמע
'Directed his heart', had intent
'Isn't it that...?', a suggested reading used to make a challenge

phrases.english: They challenged him: If one was reading in the Torah
phrases.notes: He was reading the section of שמע in the תורה.

phrases.english: and the time for reciting [Shema] arrived,
if he directed his heart, he has fulfilled [his obligation],
and if not, he has not fulfilled it.
Isn't it that he directed his heart to fulfill the obligation?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle stated in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's principle that מצוות אין צריכות כוונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes fulfilling קריאת שמע depend on 'directing the heart', which seems to mean intent to fulfill, so intent is required

steps.title: Intent to read, not intent to fulfill
steps.stepSummary: No, 'directed his heart' means he intended to read the words, not to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means he intended to read.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by reading the משנה differently. The intent the משנה requires is only the intent to read the words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of intent: intent to do the act, and intent to fulfill the מצוה. רבא only says the second kind is not needed. So a משנה that requires the first kind does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: To read, meaning intent to do the act of reading
To fulfill one's obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two kinds of intent separate: intending to perform the act (לקרות) and intending to fulfill the מצוה (לצאת). רבא only says the second is unnecessary.

phrases.english: No: [he directed his heart] to read.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by reinterpreting 'כוון לבו'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the intent is to read, not to fulfill
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Directed his heart' means intent to fulfill the מצוה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Directed his heart' means intent to read the words

steps.title: But he is already reading
steps.stepSummary: How can the משנה mean intent to read? It already says he is reading!
steps.simpleTranslation: To read?! But he is already reading!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The משנה already describes him as reading, so 'intent to read' seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who is reading obviously intends to read. So if the משנה's condition only means intent to read, it would always be met, and the case of 'if not' would never happen.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But he is reading!', a sharp objection that the point is already given

phrases.english: To read?! But he is reading!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'כוון לבו' means intent to read
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already says he is reading, so requiring intent to read would add nothing

steps.title: He was reading to check the scroll
steps.stepSummary: The case is someone reading to check the scroll for mistakes, so he is not really reading the words properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is someone reading in order to correct the scroll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case so that 'intent to read' makes sense. A person checking a scroll looks at the letters but is not truly reading the words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone proofreading focuses on the spelling and does not say the words in the normal way. For him, 'directing his heart' means switching to real reading. So the משנה requires intent to read, not intent to fulfill, and רבא's principle survives this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: To correct, checking a scroll for mistakes

phrases.english: [The case is] one who is reading in order to correct [the scroll].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to someone checking the scroll
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone reading already has intent to read, so the condition is meaningless
steps.terutzMaskana: A proofreader is not truly reading, so he needs intent to read, which fits רבא
steps.whatToRemember: The first challenge to רבא is pushed off: the משנה only requires intent to read, because the case is someone checking the scroll.

steps.title: Challenge from hearing שופר outside the בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says that someone who hears שופר or מגילה from outside the בית הכנסת fulfills the obligation only if he directed his heart. Doesn't that mean intent to fulfill?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone was passing behind a בית הכנסת, or his house was next to it, and he heard the sound of שופר or מגילה, if he directed his heart he fulfilled it, and if not, he did not. Doesn't that mean he directed his heart to fulfill the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רבא, this time from our own משנה. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'checking the scroll' answer does not seem to work, because the person is only hearing, not reading. He clearly hears the sounds, so the missing ingredient seems to be intent to fulfill. That would again mean מצוות צריכות כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear', introducing a source as a proof or challenge
Behind the בית הכנסת, outside the building
The sound of the מגילה being read on פורים

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיָה עוֹבֵר אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: Come and hear: If one was passing behind a synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ סָמוּךְ לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: or his house was next to the synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁמַע קוֹל שׁוֹפָר אוֹ קוֹל מְגִילָּה,
phrases.english: and he heard the sound of the shofar or the sound of the Megillah,
if he directed his heart, he has fulfilled [his obligation],
and if not, he has not fulfilled it.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, אִם כִּוֵּון לִבּוֹ לָצֵאת?
phrases.english: Isn't it that [it means] if he directed his heart to fulfill the obligation?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיָה עוֹבֵר אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, brings a new challenge against the same principle from step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's principle that מצוות אין צריכות כוונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The person hears the sounds, yet fulfilling depends on 'directing his heart', which seems to mean intent to fulfill

steps.title: Directed his heart means intent to hear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'directed his heart' in the משנה means he meant to hear the sound, not that he meant to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means he intended to hear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by explaining the משנה's words a different way. 'Directed his heart' only means he meant to hear the שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 7 read 'directed his heart' as intent to fulfill the מצוה. The answer says it is only intent to hear the sound. That is a much lower bar, so the משנה no longer proves that a מצוה needs intent.

keyTerms.meaning: To hear. Here it means meaning to hear the sound.
No. The גמרא is rejecting the reading suggested in the challenge.

phrases.english: No, it means he intended to hear.
phrases.notes: This answers Step 7: the משנה's 'directed his heart' is about the hearing itself, not about doing the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה about שופר and מגילה heard from outside.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Directed his heart' means intent to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Directed his heart' means only intent to hear the sound.

steps.title: But he already heard it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה could mean 'intent to hear', since it already says he heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: To hear?! But he did hear!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. The משנה already says he heard the שופר, so why add that he intended to hear?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case is someone who heard the sound. If 'directed his heart' only means intending to hear, those words seem to add nothing. This is the same kind of question as Step 5 about reading the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: But he did hear!

phrases.english: To hear?! But he did hear!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'directed his heart' as intent to hear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already says he heard, so 'intent to hear' would add nothing to the משנה's words.

steps.title: He thought it was just a donkey
steps.stepSummary: The case is someone who heard the sound but thought it was only a donkey braying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought it was just a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains when someone hears but has no 'intent to hear': he hears the noise but thinks it is a donkey, not a שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can hear a sound without knowing it is a שופר. The משנה teaches that such a person does not fulfill the מצוה. Knowing it is a שופר is enough, even without intent to fulfill the מצוה, so רבא's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought, he assumed.
A donkey.
Merely, just.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'intent to hear a שופר' with 'intent to fulfill the מצוה'. According to רבא, only the first is needed.

phrases.english: He thought it was just a donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by describing a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone who heard the sound also intended to hear.
steps.terutzMaskana: Someone can hear without knowing it is a שופר, so 'intent to hear' does add something.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא requiring intent from blower and listener
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says both the listener and the blower need intent. The case of a blower without intent seems to be someone blowing for music, which suggests intent to fulfill the מצוה is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If the listener had intent but the blower did not, or the blower had intent but the listener did not, he has not fulfilled the מצוה until both the listener and the blower have intent. It makes sense that the blower had intent and the listener did not, if the listener thought it was just a donkey. But when the listener had intent and the blower did not, how could that happen? Isn't it where he blows for music?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבא. The ברייתא says the blower must also have intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listener without intent fits the 'donkey' explanation. But a blower knows he is blowing a שופר, so the donkey idea cannot explain him. His lack of intent seems to mean he was blowing for music, and then the listener does not fulfill the מצוה. That suggests intent to fulfill the מצוה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged him with a source.
The listener.
The one who makes others hear, meaning the blower.
He has not fulfilled his obligation.
Blowing for music.
How could this case happen?

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the strongest proof so far that a מצוה needs intent, because the 'donkey' answer cannot work for the blower.

phrases.english: They challenged him:
If the listener had intent but the blower did not,
or the blower had intent but the listener did not,
he has not fulfilled his obligation,
until both the listener and the blower have intent.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא נִתְכַּוֵּון מַשְׁמִיעַ וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון שׁוֹמֵעַ —
phrases.english: It makes sense where the blower had intent but the listener did not:
that is where he thought it was just a donkey.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נִתְכַּוֵּון שׁוֹמֵעַ וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון מַשְׁמִיעַ —
phrases.english: But where the listener had intent and the blower did not,
how could that case happen?
Isn't it where he blows for music?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: נִתְכַּוֵּון שׁוֹמֵעַ וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון מַשְׁמִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source against רבא's view after the משנה was explained away.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that מצוות אין צריכות כוונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blower without intent cannot be thinking 'it's a donkey'. The only likely case is blowing for music, and then the listener does not fulfill the מצוה, so intent to fulfill the מצוה is needed.

steps.title: Perhaps he was making barking sounds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the blower without intent may have been making barking noises rather than proper blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is where he was making barking sounds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The blower 'without intent' may simply not have been trying to blow real שופר sounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'intent' for the blower may only mean intent to blow proper sounds. If he just made random barking noises, those are not real שופר sounds at all. So the ברייתא does not prove that a מצוה needs intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps.
Making barking sounds, meaning random blasts that are not proper שופר sounds.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is where he was making barking sounds.
phrases.notes: The blower was just making noise with the שופר, not blowing the proper sounds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof from the ברייתא in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא is talking about blowing for music.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is another possible case: improper barking blasts. There, the missing 'intent' is about blowing proper sounds, not about fulfilling the מצוה.

steps.title: אביי: sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: if intent is not needed, then sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת counts as adding to the מצוה, and the person should get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But if so, someone who sleeps in the סוכה on the eighth day should get lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new challenge from what people actually do. Outside ארץ ישראל people sit in the סוכה on the eighth day too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מצוה counts even without intent, then sitting in the סוכה on the eighth day automatically counts as a מצוה action. That would break the איסור of בל תוסיף, adding to a מצוה, which is punished with lashes. Yet people do sit in the סוכה on the eighth day, so it seems a מצוה does need intent.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so. This opens a challenge showing a strange result of the other side's view.
The eighth day, שמיני עצרת.
He should get lashes.

steps.whyThisMatters: This links the question of intent to בל תוסיף, the איסור against adding to a מצוה.

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to רבא, who holds that a מצוה does not need intent.

phrases.english: But if so,
someone who sleeps in the סוכה on the eighth day
should get lashes!
phrases.notes: He would be adding to the מצוה of sitting in the סוכה for seven days, which breaks בל תוסיף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source-based challenges were answered, אביי brings a logical challenge from בל תוסיף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that מצוות אין צריכות כוונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without needing intent, every act in the סוכה counts as a מצוה. Doing it on the eighth day would then be adding to the מצוה, which is punished with lashes. But people do it, so the view seems wrong.

steps.title: רבא: You Only Break the Rule of Adding During the מצוה's Time
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers אביי. בל תוסיף applies only when you add during the מצוה's proper time. On שמיני עצרת the סוכה time is over, so sleeping there adds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Because I hold that a person only breaks the rule of adding to מצוות during their proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's challenge from Step 13. Sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת is not adding to the מצוה, because the סוכה time is already over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that without intent, any extra sitting in the סוכה should count as adding to the מצוה. רבא limits בל תוסיף to the מצוה's own time window. After סוכות ends, sitting in a סוכה is just sitting in a hut.

keyTerms.meaning: Because I say, meaning 'my view is'
Transgresses, breaks a rule
In their proper time
The prohibition against adding to a מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This time limit on בל תוסיף is the rule the rest of this section tests.

phrases.english: He said to him: Because I say:
phrases.notes: רבא is answering אביי's question from the last step.

phrases.english: regarding מצוות, one does not transgress them
phrases.notes: He means breaking the rule against adding to a מצוה.

phrases.english: except in their proper time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the prohibition to the מצוה's time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any extra performance of a מצוה, at any time, would count as adding to it
steps.terutzMaskana: Adding is only forbidden during the מצוה's set time, so sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת is fine

steps.title: Challenge from the כהן Who Adds His Own Blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא quotes a ברייתא. A כהן may not add his own blessing to ברכת כהנים. That seems to happen after the blessing is done, when the time is over, yet the ברייתא says he breaks the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא objected from a ברייתא: How do we know that a כהן who goes up to bless should not say, 'Since the תורה let me bless ישראל, I will add a blessing of my own, like "May ה׳, the God of your fathers, increase you"'? Because the פסוק says, 'Do not add to the word.' But here, once he has finished blessing, the time is over, and still it teaches that he breaks the rule!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמן בר אבא challenges רבא with a ברייתא about a כהן who adds an extra blessing. It seems to show that you can break בל תוסיף even after the מצוה's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the כהן violates 'לא תוסיפו' by adding a blessing. The challenger assumes the addition comes after ברכת כהנים is finished, when its time has passed. By רבא's rule there should be no violation, yet the ברייתא says there is.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source
The platform where the כהנים stand to bless
Permission
Do not add, the source of בל תוסיף
It teaches, it states

phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba raised an objection:
From where do we know that a כהן who goes up to the platform,
phrases.notes: He goes up to say ברכת כהנים.

phrases.english: should not say:
Since the Torah gave me
permission to bless the Jewish people,
I will add one blessing of my own,
for example: 'May the Lord, God of your fathers, increase you'?
phrases.notes: דברים 1:11

phrases.english: The verse says: 'You shall not add to the word.'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:2

phrases.english: But here, once he has already blessed,
its time has passed,
and yet it teaches that he transgressed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's rule from Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that בל תוסיף applies only during the מצוה's time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats an addition made after ברכת כהנים is finished as breaking בל תוסיף, even though the time has passed

steps.title: The כהן Had Not Finished Yet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a כהן who added before finishing ברכת כהנים, so the מצוה's time was still running.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he had not finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. The כהן in the ברייתא added his blessing before he finished, so it was still during the מצוה's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the addition came after the blessing was done. The גמרא changes the case to an addition in the middle of ברכת כהנים. That fits רבא's rule perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Finished, completed

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where he did not finish.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן added his blessing in the middle of ברכת כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן added after finishing, outside the מצוה's time
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן added before finishing, during the מצוה's time

steps.title: But a ברייתא Says He Did Finish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a ברייתא says outright that the כהן had finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'he finished'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. A ברייתא clearly describes a כהן who had already finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said the כהן had not finished. A version of the ברייתא says 'סיים,' that he finished. So the problem with רבא's rule seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But it is taught: 'He finished'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כהן had not finished
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says the כהן finished, so the addition seems to come after the time

steps.title: He Finished Only One of the Blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'he finished' means he finished one of the three blessings of ברכת כהנים. He was still in the middle of the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He finished one blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'finished' means the כהן finished only the first of the three blessings. So he was still in the middle of the מצוה when he added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת כהנים has three parts. Finishing one part does not end the מצוה, so its time is still running. רבא's rule stands: adding is forbidden only during the מצוה's time.

keyTerms.meaning: One blessing, one of the three פסוקים of ברכת כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: רבא holds that בל תוסיף applies only during a מצוה's time. The case of the כהן adding a blessing is explained as an addition in the middle of ברכת כהנים, after only one of its three blessings.
steps.confusionAlert: 'סיים' here does not mean he finished all of ברכת כהנים. It means he finished just the first of its three blessings.

phrases.english: He finished one blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He finished' means he finished all of ברכת כהנים
steps.terutzMaskana: 'He finished' means he finished one blessing, so he was still within the מצוה's time

steps.title: A ברייתא says he finished all his blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 18 with a ברייתא that says the כהן finished all of his blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: he finished all his blessings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. That answer said 'finished' meant finishing only one blessing, but another ברייתא clearly says he finished all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 saved רבא's rule by saying the כהן was still in the middle of ברכת כהנים. This ברייתא says 'all his blessings', so he was fully done. Then the time of the מצוה seems to be over, yet he still breaks בל תוסיף, which seems to go against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (opens a challenge)
He finished
All of his blessings (all three parts of ברכת כהנים)

phrases.english: But it was taught: he finished all his blessings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 18's reading of 'finished' as finishing only one blessing.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 18's claim that the כהן was still in the middle of ברכת כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says he finished ALL the blessings. So the מצוה's time seems over, and רבא's rule (no בל תוסיף after the time) looks contradicted.

steps.title: For ברכת כהנים the whole day is its time
steps.stepSummary: ברכת כהנים is different: a כהן who meets another צבור may bless again, so the entire day counts as the מצוה's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different. If another congregation happens to come his way, he blesses again. So the whole day is its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. ברכת כהנים is not over when the כהן finishes, because he could still bless another צבור that same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule stays the same: בל תוסיף only applies while it is still the מצוה's time. What changes is how long that time lasts. Since the כהן may repeat ברכת כהנים for a new צבור all day, adding a blessing after finishing still happens 'in its time'.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different
It happens to come his way
Another congregation
The whole day is its time

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel רבא's rule. It keeps the rule and only shows that for ברכת כהנים the 'time' stretches across the whole day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that a מצוה you are allowed to repeat stays 'in its time', which the גמרא now wants to prove.

phrases.english: Here it is different,
since if there happens to come to him
another congregation,
he blesses again —
the whole day is its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּאִלּוּ מִתְרְמֵי לֵיהּ צִבּוּרָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by widening the time-frame of ברכת כהנים instead of rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the time of this מצוה lasts all day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the כהן finished all the blessings, the מצוה's time was over, so בל תוסיף should not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since he could bless another צבור, the whole day is the time of ברכת כהנים, so adding is still 'in its time'.

steps.title: Where do we learn this? A משנה about mixed blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source and begins quoting a משנה about blood of קרבנות that got mixed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say this? As we learned in a משנה: blood that needs one sprinkling that got mixed with blood that needs one sprinkling is sprinkled once. Blood that needs four sprinklings mixed with blood that needs four sprinklings is sprinkled four times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that a מצוה you may repeat stays 'in its time', and starts quoting a משנה to prove it. These opening cases are setup; the argument that matters comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some קרבנות need their blood put on the מזבח once, and others need four placings. When two bloods of the same kind mix, there is no problem: you just do what both need. The easy cases set the stage for the hard case of a mix between four and one.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asks for a source)
As we learned in a משנה
One placing (sprinkling) of blood on the מזבח
Four placings of blood on the מזבח
Got mixed together

phrases.english: And from where do you say this —
As we learned: those placed with one placing,
phrases.notes: The משנה is talking about the blood of קרבנות put on the מזבח.

phrases.english: that got mixed with those placed with one placing —
should be placed with one placing.
Four placings mixed with four placings —
should be placed with four placings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a source for the idea in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a מצוה you may repeat counts as still in its time
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about blood of קרבנות that got mixed together

steps.title: The argument: four placings mixed with one
steps.stepSummary: When blood needing four placings mixes with blood needing one, רבי אליעזר says to place four times and רבי יהושע says to place once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four placings mixed with one placing: רבי אליעזר says, place it four times. רבי יהושע says, place it once.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה reaches the hard case, where the two bloods need different numbers of placings, and gives two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever you do, one of the bloods gets the wrong number. רבי אליעזר goes with the bigger number so nothing is missing. רבי יהושע goes with the smaller number so nothing extra is done.

keyTerms.meaning: תנא who says to place four times
תנא who says to place once
They should be placed (on the מזבח)

phrases.english: Four placings mixed with one placing,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
they should be placed with four placings,
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
they should be placed with one placing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתַּן אַרְבַּע בְּמַתַּן אַחַת, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה, moving from the easy cases to the disputed one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four placings mixed with one: רבי אליעזר says four placings, רבי יהושע says one placing.

steps.title: Each side warns the other: בל תגרע versus בל תוסיף
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says placing once breaks בל תגרע. רבי יהושע answers that placing four times breaks בל תוסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: But he breaks 'do not take away'! רבי יהושע said to him: But he breaks 'do not add'!
steps.whatsHappening: Each תנא attacks the other's view. One worries about doing too little, the other about doing too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you place once, the קרבן that needs four is missing three, which is בל תגרע. If you place four times, the קרבן that needs one gets three extra, which is בל תוסיף. This shows extra placings for a מצוה can count as בל תוסיף, which is what the גמרא will build its proof on.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not take away from a מצוה
Do not add to a מצוה
Breaks (a prohibition)

steps.whatToRemember: In mixed blood, רבי אליעזר fears בל תגרע (too little), and רבי יהושע fears בל תוסיף (too much). The גמרא is using this משנה to back up the idea that a מצוה you may repeat is still in its time.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
But he breaks 'do not take away'!
phrases.notes: דברים 13:1. Placing only once leaves the four-placing קרבן short.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
But he breaks 'do not add'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תִּגְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives each תנא's reason for his view in Step 22, as challenges to the other side.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Placing once takes away from the four-placing קרבן (בל תגרע). Placing four times adds to the one-placing קרבן (בל תוסיף).

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Do Not Add Only Applies to Unmixed Blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע's attack: בל תוסיף only applies when the blood is by itself, not when it is mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: The rule 'Do not add' was only said for blood that stands by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his view that we should place the blood four times. He answers רבי יהושע's claim that doing so breaks בל תוסיף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says the ban on adding only applies when the blood is unmixed. In a mixture, the extra placings are needed for the other blood. So placing four times breaks no rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on adding to a מצוה
Was said (in the תורה)
By itself, not mixed

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
'Do not add' was not said
except when it is by itself.
phrases.notes: "It" means the blood standing on its own, not mixed with other blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: לֹא נֶאֱמַר בַּל תּוֹסִיף אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's argument from Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Placing four times breaks בל תוסיף for the one-placing blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: בל תוסיף applies only to unmixed blood, so a mixture is not covered.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Do Not Diminish Also Only Applies to Unmixed Blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע turns the same logic around: בל תגרע also only applies to unmixed blood, so placing once is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: The rule 'Do not diminish' was also only said for blood that stands by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע uses רבי אליעזר's own reasoning to defend placing only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If mixed blood is not covered by בל תוסיף, then it is not covered by בל תגרע either. So רבי אליעזר's attack from Step 23 fails too. Now the two sides are even, and neither argument decides the case.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on taking away from a מצוה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
'Do not diminish' was not said
except when it is by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לֹא נֶאֱמַר בַּל תִּגְרַע אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors רבי אליעזר's answer from Step 24 to protect רבי יהושע's own view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel argument (same logic applied to the other side)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Placing once breaks בל תגרע for the four-placing blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: בל תגרע also applies only to unmixed blood, so placing once is allowed.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Better to Break a Rule Passively Than Actively
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע adds a second argument: not placing breaks a rule without an action, but placing extra breaks a rule with an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said further: When you do not place the blood, you break 'Do not diminish' but you did nothing with your hand. When you place it, you break 'Do not add' and you did something with your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives one more reason to place only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if both rules might apply, the two violations are not equal. Leaving out placings is only a failure to act. Adding placings is an active wrong, so placing once is the better choice.

keyTerms.meaning: And further (an extra argument)
You placed (the blood)
An act done with your own hand

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's view: placing four times is an active violation of בל תוסיף, and that is worse than passively leaving out placings.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua said further:
When you did not place,
phrases.notes: He means: when you did not place the blood four times.

phrases.english: you transgressed 'do not diminish'
but you did not do an act with your hand;
when you placed,
you transgressed 'do not add'
and you did an act with your hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second argument for רבי יהושע after the two sides were evened out in Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: Placing only once is the better choice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that a passive violation is lighter than an active one.

steps.title: The Proof: The Whole Day Counts as the Time for Sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that after the בכור's one placing, its time seems to be over, yet רבי יהושע says an extra placing breaks בל תוסיף. That must be because another בכור could come later that day, so the whole day is its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, once he has given the placing of the firstborn, its time has passed, and yet the משנה teaches that he transgresses 'Do not add.' Is it not because we say that if another firstborn came his way, he would sprinkle again, so the whole day is its time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the משנה it just quoted as the source it asked for in Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the בכור's single placing is done, its מצוה seems finished. Even so, רבי יהושע says extra placings break בל תוסיף. The גמרא explains this by the fact that another בכור could still be offered that day, which makes the whole day the מצוה's time, just like ברכת כהנים in Step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: A placing of blood on the מזבח
A firstborn animal brought as a קרבן (its blood needs one placing)
Its time
Happens to come his way
Sprinkles

phrases.english: And here,
once he has given the placing of the firstborn,
its time has passed,
and it teaches that he transgresses 'do not add.'
Is it not because we say:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ מִתְרְמֵי לֵיהּ בּוּכְרָא אַחֲרִינָא —
phrases.english: since if another firstborn happened to come to him,
he would sprinkle from it again,
the whole day is its time?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ מַתָּנָה מִבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה from Steps 21-26 as proof for the principle from Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: If a מצוה can be repeated later that day, the entire day counts as its time.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's ruling that extra placings after the בכור's one placing break בל תוסיף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This would give the principle from Step 20 a source beyond ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: Rejection: Maybe רבי יהושע Holds Do Not Add Applies Even After the Time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: maybe רבי יהושע holds that בל תוסיף applies even outside a מצוה's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps רבי יהושע holds that one transgresses by adding to מצוות even outside their time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the proof from Step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that בל תוסיף only applies during a מצוה's time. But maybe רבי יהושע holds that it applies even after the time is over. If so, his ruling says nothing about the whole day being the time, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do you know)?
Perhaps
He holds
Outside their proper time

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's ruling alone does not prove that the whole day is the time, because he may hold that בל תוסיף applies even outside a מצוה's time. The next steps rebuild the proof in a different way.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the principle from Step 20 is wrong. It only says this משנה cannot prove it.

phrases.english: From where [do you know this]?
Perhaps Rabbi Yehoshua holds
that one transgresses [by adding] to מצוות
even outside their time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof, not the principle itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes רבי יהושע limits בל תוסיף to a מצוה's time, but he may apply it even after the time.

steps.title: Why did רב שמן בר אבא skip the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its real point: why did רב שמן בר אבא challenge from a ברייתא and not from the משנה about the blood?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we meant: why did רב שמן בר אבא leave the משנה and challenge from a ברייתא? He should have challenged from the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how its proof really works. The proof does not come from רבי יהושע's ruling itself. It comes from asking why רב שמן בר אבא picked the ברייתא and not the משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 pushed away the proof from the משנה. Now the גמרא says it was really asking a different question. A משנה is the stronger and better-known source, so we would expect רב שמן בר אבא to quote it first.

keyTerms.meaning: leaves aside, skips
raises a challenge
a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: This is what we were saying:

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא מַאי טַעְמָא
phrases.english: What is the reason that Rav Shemen bar Abba
set aside the mishna
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about placing the blood of a בכור, from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: and raised a challenge from a baraita?
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא about a כהן who adds a blessing of his own to ברכת כהנים.

phrases.english: Let him challenge from the mishna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Recasts why the משנה was brought, after step 28 pushed away the proof from it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב שמן בר אבא chose the ברייתא as his source and not the משנה.

steps.title: The משנה can be pushed off
steps.stepSummary: He did not use the משנה because another בכור might come that day, so the whole day is the time of the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why didn't he challenge from the משנה? Because if another בכור came to him, he would have to place its blood. So the whole day is its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The משנה is easy to push off, so רב שמן בר אבא avoided it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra placing of blood is not truly 'outside its time.' Another בכור could arrive that same day, so the whole day is the time for placing blood. That makes the משנה a weak source for a question about breaking a מצוה outside its time.

keyTerms.meaning: happens to come his way
a firstborn animal (בכור)
its proper time

phrases.english: Why does he not challenge from the mishna?
Because if there happened to come to him
another firstborn,
he would need to sprinkle its blood,
so the whole day is its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה can be deflected because the whole day is the time for placing blood.

steps.title: The ברייתא can be pushed off the same way
steps.stepSummary: The same reasoning should work for ברכת כהנים: another group could come, so the whole day is its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא too: if another congregation came, he would bless again. So the whole day is its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues that the ברייתא is no better than the משנה. It can be pushed off in exactly the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who already blessed once could meet another congregation that same day and bless them. By the same logic, the whole day would be the time for ברכת כהנים. Then a blessing he adds after finishing is still 'in its time,' and רב שמן בר אבא's challenge falls apart. This is the proof for the idea from step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: a congregation
goes back and blesses again

phrases.english: The baraita too:
since if there happened to come
another congregation,
he would bless again,
so the whole day is its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 30 against the ברייתא as well.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמן בר אבא's choice to challenge from the ברייתא about ברכת כהנים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'whole day is its time' reasoning that weakens the משנה should weaken the ברייתא too.

steps.title: Required versus optional
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how רב שמן בר אבא would answer: placing blood is required, but blessing a second congregation is optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שמן בר אבא? There, he has no choice but to place the blood. Here, if he wants he blesses, and if he wants he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב שמן בר אבא would see the two cases as different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the בכור, if another animal comes, placing its blood is a must. So the whole day truly is its time. With ברכת כהנים, a כהן must bless only once a day, and blessing another congregation is up to him. So after the first blessing, its time really is over.

keyTerms.meaning: there is no way around it, it must be done
if he wants

steps.whyThisMatters: Something counts as 'its time' only if the obligation still applies, not just because the act is allowed.

phrases.english: And Rav Shemen bar Abba?
phrases.notes: He means: how would רב שמן בר אבא answer this?

phrases.english: There, he cannot avoid placing it.
Here, if he wants, he blesses;
if he wants, he does not bless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases treat the whole day as the time of the מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a required act keeps the whole day as its time. An optional second blessing does not.

steps.title: רבא: breaking a מצוה needs כוונה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers in a new way: doing a מצוה needs no כוונה, but breaking it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: to fulfill a מצוה, you do not need כוונה. To break it, you need כוונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to אביי's challenge about sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת. This answer does not rely on the 'only in its time' rule that רב שמן בר אבא attacked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone can fulfill a מצוה even without meaning to. But he only breaks בל תוסיף or בל תגרע if he means to do the act as a מצוה. So a person sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת without that כוונה breaks nothing, while the כהן who deliberately adds a blessing does transgress.

keyTerms.meaning: to fulfill your obligation
to break a law
intent to do the act as a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Doing a מצוה and breaking a מצוה are not mirror images. רבא treats them differently when it comes to כוונה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
To fulfill, one does not need intent;
to transgress, one needs intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבא אמר לצאת לא בעי כוונה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the משנה/ברייתא discussion and gives a different answer to אביי's challenge from step 13. This answer avoids the time-based rule that רב שמן בר אבא challenged.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a מצוה counts without כוונה, sleeping in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת automatically breaks בל תוסיף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without כוונה, there is no transgression.

steps.title: The blood case breaks the rule without כוונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: according to רבי יהושע, extra blood breaks בל תוסיף even without כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the placing of blood, according to רבי יהושע, is a case where one transgresses without needing כוונה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's rule using רבי יהושע's view from the earlier steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע says that placing extra blood breaks בל תוסיף. He does not require that the person meant it as a מצוה. That goes against רבא's claim that breaking a מצוה always needs כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: placing the blood on the altar

phrases.english: But the placing of blood according to Rabbi Yehoshua
is a case of transgressing without needing intent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rule from step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that breaking a מצוה needs כוונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע holds that extra blood breaks בל תוסיף with no mention of כוונה.

steps.title: רבא refines his rule: in its time or not
steps.stepSummary: Breaking a מצוה during its time needs no כוונה. Breaking it outside its time does need כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: to fulfill, no כוונה is needed. To transgress during its time, no כוונה is needed. Outside its time, כוונה is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא changes his rule so that it fits רבי יהושע's view on the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra placing of blood happens during the time of the מצוה, so it breaks בל תוסיף even without כוונה. Sleeping in a סוכה on שמיני עצרת is outside the time of the מצוה. There he only breaks בל תוסיף if he does it with כוונה for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: during its proper time
not during its proper time

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final rule: doing a מצוה never needs כוונה. Breaking it during its time needs no כוונה. Breaking it outside its time needs כוונה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
To fulfill, one does not need intent.
To transgress during its time, one does not need intent;
not during its time, one needs intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Revises רבא's rule from step 33 in light of the קשיא in step 34.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Breaking בל תוסיף during the time of a מצוה needs no כוונה. Outside its time, it needs כוונה.

steps.title: רבי זירא speaks to his attendant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces something רבי זירא told his attendant about intent when blowing שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to his attendant:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It tells us that רבי זירא spoke to his attendant, and his actual words come right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line gives no ruling yet. It only names the speaker and who he spoke to. Because it comes right after the discussion of כוונה in מצוות, his instruction will connect to whether blowing שופר for someone else needs כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him
An אמורא who is the speaker here
His attendant, the person who served him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a ruling in this line. It is only the opening of a story, and the instruction itself comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to his attendant:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the conclusion about כוונה in step 35, the גמרא brings a story involving רבי זירא that relates to כוונה when blowing שופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces רבי זירא's instruction to his attendant.
